name: Sapo National Park
blurb: Liberia's rainforest: forest elephants, pygmy hippos and chimpanzees.

tip.title: Lose the forest elephants
tip.text: Elephants spread seeds from many trees. Set African forest elephant to -100% and watch the fruit and canopy trees, then the animals that eat from them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Fig trees of the forest. Their fruit is a staple for forest birds and primates; Wikipedia lists figs as a key food of the black-casqued hornbill.

nodes.name: African ebony & relatives
nodes.desc: Diospyros trees recorded repeatedly in the park area by GBIF. Their fleshy fruit is food for forest animals.
Eats bark, leaves and fruit and spreads seeds in its dung, sometimes over 5 km. Wikipedia calls it the megagardener of the forest.
A forest duiker that is locally abundant in Sapo and the most recorded duiker in the park area.
Endangered monkey of the canopy. Eats mainly fruit, blossoms and leaves, plus some insects. Leopards, crowned eagles and chimpanzees prey on it.
A leaf-eating canopy monkey recorded in the park area. It is hunted by chimpanzees in other West African forests.
About 90 percent fruit, with figs and oil palm fruit as staples. An important seed disperser of forest trees.

nodes.name: Western chimpanzee
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal in the park area, with a population estimated at 500 to 1,640. Eats fruit and hunts monkeys such as colobus.
An omnivore eating fruit, small animals, insects and carrion. Its latrines may help spread seeds.
Unusually for a raptor it eats mostly fruit, but also takes crabs, fish and carrion. GloBI has a record of it feeding on a buffalo.

nodes.name: African leopard
nodes.desc: The top mammal predator of Sapo. In African rainforests it mostly eats duikers and primates, and it also scavenges.
A forest eagle whose most common prey is monkeys. It also takes duikers.
Wet season from May to October and dry season from November to April set the rhythm of fruiting and growth.
Canopy trees about 25 m high intercept most of the light, leaving the forest floor shaded.
Soil holds the nutrients recycled from fallen leaves and dead animals.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
